title: Abraham's Journey of Faith
summary: From Ur of the Chaldeans to the land God promised, following Abraham's travels in Genesis.

stops.note: Terah takes Abram, Sarai and Lot out of Ur of the Chaldeans.
The family settles in Haran, where Terah dies.
God appears: "To your offspring I will give this land." Abram builds an altar.
Abram pitches his tent between Bethel and Ai and calls on the LORD.
Famine drives Abram down to Egypt.
Abram returns to the altar at Bethel; he and Lot separate.
Abram settles by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron.
Abraham sojourns in Gerar with King Abimelech.
Covenant with Abimelech at Beersheba.
God tests Abraham: the offering of Isaac on Mount Moriah.
Sarah dies at Hebron and is buried in the cave of Machpelah.

title: The Exodus & Wilderness Wanderings
summary: Israel leaves Egypt, meets God at Sinai, and wanders until reaching the plains of Moab. Many wilderness sites are uncertain; locations follow OpenBible.info's best identifications.

stops.note: The people of Israel set out from Rameses.
First camp at Succoth.
Camp at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness; the pillar of cloud and fire leads them.
Camp by the sea at Pi-hahiroth; God parts the sea (Exod 14:21-22).
Bitter water made sweet.
Twelve springs and seventy palm trees.
Wilderness of Sin: God sends manna and quail.
Water from the rock; victory over Amalek.
Israel camps before the mountain; the Law is given.
The twelve spies report back; Israel refuses to enter and is sentenced to 40 years of wandering.
Aaron dies on Mount Hor.
Israel camps in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho.
Moses views the Promised Land from Mount Nebo and dies.

title: The Conquest of Canaan
summary: Under Joshua, Israel crosses the Jordan and takes the land in a central, southern and northern campaign.

stops.note: Joshua sends two spies from Shittim to Jericho.
Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground and camps at Gilgal.
The walls fall down flat; Jericho is taken.
After Achan's sin is dealt with, Ai is taken.
Joshua builds an altar and reads the Law.
Joshua defends Gibeon; the sun stands still.
The enemy flees down the pass of Beth-horon under a storm of hailstones.
Southern campaign: Makkedah taken.
Libnah taken.
Lachish taken on the second day.
Eglon taken.
Hebron taken.
Debir taken.
Joshua returns to camp at Gilgal.
Northern campaign: the kings gather at the waters of Merom and are defeated.
Hazor, head of the northern kingdoms, is burned.
The tabernacle is set up at Shiloh; the land is divided among the tribes.

title: The Life & Ministry of Jesus
summary: Key places in the life of Jesus, in an approximate harmony of the four Gospels. Exact order of some Galilean events is debated.

stops.note: Jesus is born in Bethlehem, the city of David.
Joseph flees with Mary and the child to Egypt.
The family settles in Nazareth.
At twelve, Jesus stays behind in the temple.
Baptized by John at Bethany beyond the Jordan.
First sign: water turned to wine at a wedding.
A short stay in Capernaum.
Passover: Jesus cleanses the temple; meets Nicodemus.
The Samaritan woman at Jacob's well.
Heals the official's son from a distance.
Reads Isaiah in the synagogue and is rejected.
Makes Capernaum his home base; calls the fishermen.
Raises a widow's son.
Across the lake, frees a man from a legion of demons (traditional site at Kursi).
Feeds the five thousand near Bethsaida.
After walking on the water, lands at Gennesaret.
The Syrophoenician woman's faith.
Returns by way of Sidon...
...to the Sea of Galilee through the Decapolis.
Heals a blind man at Bethsaida.
"Who do you say that I am?" Peter's confession.
The temple tax and the coin in the fish's mouth.
Feast of Booths; teaches in the temple.
Raises Lazarus at Bethany near Jerusalem.
Withdraws to Ephraim, near the wilderness.
Zacchaeus; blind Bartimaeus healed.
Anointed by Mary six days before Passover.
Triumphal entry into Jerusalem.
Prays in Gethsemane and is arrested.
Crucified at Golgotha; buried nearby and raised on the third day.
The risen Jesus walks with two disciples to Emmaus.
Appears by the Sea of Tiberias and restores Peter.
Ascends to heaven near Bethany, on the Mount of Olives.

title: Paul's First Missionary Journey
summary: Paul and Barnabas are sent out from Antioch to Cyprus and southern Galatia (Acts 13–14).

stops.note: The Holy Spirit sets apart Barnabas and Saul.
They go down to the port of Seleucia.
Preach in the synagogues of Salamis on Cyprus.
Elymas the sorcerer is blinded; the proconsul believes.
John Mark leaves them and returns to Jerusalem.
Pisidian Antioch: Paul's synagogue sermon; turns to the Gentiles.
Many believe, but a plot forces them out.
A lame man healed; Paul is stoned and left for dead.
Preach the gospel and make many disciples.
Return, strengthening the disciples...
...appointing elders in every church...
...back through Pisidian Antioch.
Speak the word in Perga.
Sail from Attalia.
Report to the church at Syrian Antioch all God had done.

title: Paul's Second Missionary Journey
summary: Paul and Silas revisit the churches, then cross into Europe (Acts 15:36–18:22).

stops.note: Paul and Silas set out from Syrian Antioch.
Revisit Derbe...
...and Lystra, where Timothy joins them.
The vision of the man of Macedonia.
Sail straight to Samothrace.
Land at Neapolis.
Lydia converted; Paul and Silas jailed; the jailer believes.
Pass through Amphipolis...
...and Apollonia.
Three Sabbaths in the synagogue; a riot.
The Bereans examine the Scriptures daily.
Sermon at the Areopagus: "the unknown god".
Eighteen months with Aquila and Priscilla.
Paul cuts his hair because of a vow.
Brief visit; reasons in the synagogue.
Lands at Caesarea...
...goes up and greets the church...
...and returns to Antioch.

title: Paul's Third Missionary Journey
summary: A long ministry in Ephesus, a return through Macedonia and Greece, and the voyage to Jerusalem (Acts 18:23–21:17).

stops.note: Departs Antioch, going through Galatia and Phrygia.
Strengthening all the disciples.
Two to three years; the riot of the silversmiths.
Travels through Macedonia.
Three months in Greece (likely where Romans was written).
Sails from Philippi after Passover.
Eutychus falls from the window and is raised.
Paul walks to Assos and rejoins the ship.
Arrive at Mitylene.
Opposite Chios.
Touch at Samos.
Farewell to the Ephesian elders.
Straight course to Cos...
...then Rhodes...
...and Patara, where they change ships.
Seven days with the disciples at Tyre.
Greet the brothers at Ptolemais.
Stay with Philip the evangelist; Agabus' prophecy.
Arrives in Jerusalem, where he will be arrested.

title: Paul's Voyage to Rome
summary: As a prisoner, Paul sails for Rome, survives a shipwreck on Malta, and arrives in the capital (Acts 27–28).

stops.note: Held prisoner at Caesarea; appeals to Caesar.
Julius lets Paul visit friends at Sidon.
Transfer to an Alexandrian grain ship at Myra.
Slow going against the wind off Cnidus.
Paul warns against sailing on.
After fourteen days in the storm, shipwrecked on Malta.
Three days at Syracuse.
Arrive at Rhegium.
Land at Puteoli; a week with believers.
Brothers from Rome come to meet him...
...and Paul thanks God and takes courage.
Two years under house arrest, proclaiming the kingdom of God.
